ready1_open_rewrite.title: SciVerse open question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: In a 400 mL beaker, add 5.00g $\mathrm{PbCl_2}$ to 300 mL of water and heat for 10min. At the end of heating, some solid $\mathrm{PbCl_2}$ still remains undissolved at the bottom of the beaker. Cool the solution to room temperature overnight. The next day, take 100 mL of the saturated solution into a 250 mL beaker, being careful not to transfer any residual solid. Add 100 mL of 0.75 M KI solution, and the following precipitation reaction occurs: $\mathrm{Pb^{2+} + 2I^- \rightarrow PbI_2(s)}$. Filter and dry the $\mathrm{PbI_2}$ precipitate; its mass is 0.747g. Calculate the solubility product constant $K_{sp}$ of $\mathrm{PbCl_2}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a container with liquid inside; above is a wavy liquid surface, the liquid-phase region is labeled “Saturated PbCl2(aq)”, and there is a layer of solid region at the bottom labeled “PbCl2(s)”. This indicates that solid PbCl2 coexists with its saturated aqueous solution in the system, so the Pb2+ concentration in the saturated solution can be used to determine the Ksp of PbCl2. Reasoning: The problem states that 100 mL of saturated PbCl2 solution is taken, 100 mL of 0.75 M KI is added, PbI2(s) is formed, and the dried precipitate mass is 0.747 g. The amount of substance of I- in KI is 0.100 L × 0.75 mol/L = 0.075 mol, far greater than the I- required for about 0.0016 mol Pb2+ to precipitate, so Pb2+ can be regarded as completely precipitated. The reaction Pb2+ + 2I- → PbI2(s) shows that n(Pb2+) = n(PbI2). The molar mass of PbI2 is about 461 g/mol, so n(PbI2) = 0.747 g / 461 g/mol ≈ 1.6×10^-3 mol, which is the amount of substance of Pb2+ in the original 100 mL saturated PbCl2 solution. Thus in the original saturated solution, [Pb2+] = s ≈ (1.6×10^-3 mol)/(0.100 L) ≈ 1.6×10^-2 M. PbCl2(s) ⇌ Pb2+ + 2Cl-, so [Cl-] = 2s. Ksp = [Pb2+][Cl-]^2 = s(2s)^2 = 4s^3. Substituting s ≈ 1.6×10^-2 M gives Ksp ≈ 1.63×10^-5.

method.method_draft: 从图像确认体系是PbCl2(s)与饱和PbCl2(aq)共存。读取题文中取出的饱和液体积100 mL、加入KI的浓度和体积、PbI2沉淀质量0.747 g。先算n(PbI2)=0.747/M(PbI2)，这等于100 mL原饱和液中的n(Pb2+)；再除以0.100 L得原饱和液[Pb2+]。由PbCl2溶解产生1 mol Pb2+和2 mol Cl-，令s=[Pb2+]，代入Ksp=[Pb2+][Cl-]^2=s(2s)^2，得到约1.63×10^-5。

method.method_draft: 从图像和题文的“仍有部分固体未溶解”确认原烧杯中是室温饱和PbCl2溶液。用0.747 g PbI2计算100 mL样品对应的n(PbI2)，即100 mL中溶解的n(PbCl2)。因为样品来自300 mL均一饱和液，可将该物质的量乘以3得到原300 mL中总溶解PbCl2的摩尔数，再除以0.300 L得到PbCl2的摩尔溶解度s。最后根据溶解平衡中[Pb2+]=s、[Cl-]=2s，计算Ksp=s(2s)^2，得到约1.63×10^-5。
method.CoT_raw:
先描述图像：图中烧杯内液面下标有“Saturated PbCl2(aq)”，烧杯底部有一层固体并标有“PbCl2(s)”。这说明液体与未溶解的PbCl2固体共存，因此该溶液为PbCl2的饱和溶液。

再推理：题目中也说明加热后烧杯底部仍有部分PbCl2未溶解，冷却过夜后取上层溶液，因此所取100 mL样品是室温下的饱和PbCl2溶液。加入过量KI后，Pb2+按反应Pb2+ + 2I- -> PbI2(s)沉淀，所以生成PbI2的物质的量等于100 mL样品中Pb2+的物质的量，也等于该100 mL饱和溶液中溶解的PbCl2的物质的量。

由0.747 g PbI2计算，n(PbI2)约为1.60×10^-3 mol，因此100 mL饱和溶液中n(PbCl2)约为1.60×10^-3 mol。样品来自原300 mL均一饱和液，所以原300 mL中溶解的PbCl2为3倍，约4.79×10^-3 mol。于是PbCl2的摩尔溶解度s = n/V ≈ (4.79×10^-3 mol)/(0.300 L) ≈ 1.60×10^-2 M。

PbCl2(s) ⇌ Pb2+ + 2Cl-，所以[Pb2+] = s，[Cl-] = 2s。Ksp = [Pb2+][Cl-]^2 = s(2s)^2 = 4s^3 ≈ 4(1.60×10^-2)^3 ≈ 1.63×10^-5。
